deep.reconstruction:
This is sheet '2' of an early (1983) draft of what became the axioms for 'dérivateurs' (derivators), inside the Pursuing Stacks / homotopy-theories period. Here H is a contravariant 2-functor from Cat (small categories) to categories: A ↦ H(A), f ↦ H(f) = f^*_H.

Diagram (5) states the compatibility of the 'underlying diagram' functors. For each A there is a functor α_A : H(A) → Hom(A, Hot_H), where Hot_H plays the role of H(e), the value on the point (the 'homotopy category' of the theory). It sends an object of H(A) to its diagram of fibres. For f : A → B the square formed by H(f), α_B, α_A and the bottom map f^* (precomposition with f) commutes. This is the standard 'dia' functor of derivator theory.

(Der 1): if A = ∐_{i∈I} A_i, then H(A) → ∏ H(A_i) is an isomorphism. This is the coproduct axiom of derivators. A second axiom, circled '(2)', is only begun with a parenthesis I read as '(intégration?)' or similar, and is left empty.

The rest of the page is crossed out. It records an abandoned formulation of the existence of homotopy left Kan extensions.
- For each A one is given L_A : H(A) → H(A^), where ε_A : A ↪ A^ is 'the canonical inclusion'.
- (7) requires (ε_A)^*_H ∘ L_A = id_{H(A)}.
- Der 3 then demands, for every f : A → B, a functor f_! : H(A) → H(B) such that, up to isomorphism, L_B ∘ f_! ≅ (f^*_∧)^*_H ∘ L_A. The right vertical map is defined as f̂_! := (f^*_∧)^*_H.

The most coherent reading takes A^ = Â, the presheaf category, with ε_A the Yoneda embedding and f^*_∧ : B̂ → Â the restriction of presheaves along f. Pulling back along this functor gives a covariant map H(Â) → H(B̂), as the diagram requires. L_A is then a 'Yoneda / colimit-preserving extension' that restricts back to the identity because Yoneda is fully faithful. f_! is recovered as f_! = ε_B^* ∘ (f^*)^*_H ∘ L_A.

Check in the represented case H(A) = Fun(A, C) with C cocomplete:
- L_A F = Lan_y F, i.e. P ↦ P ⊗_A F.
- Then (f^*)^* L_A F (P) = f^*P ⊗_A F.
- Restricting to representables gives b ↦ B(f−, b) ⊗_A F = (Lan_f F)(b), the usual coend formula for the left Kan extension.
- The required square L_B f_! ≅ (f^*)^* L_A holds by coend calculus.

So the abandoned axiom encodes Kan extension along f as 'pullback along the right adjoint f^* : B̂ → Â, transported through the Yoneda extension'. Equivalently, the fact that u ⊣ v gives v^* ⊣ u^* lets one turn the adjunction f_! ⊣ f^* on presheaves into homotopy-level functors.

An alternative reading is A^ = A with a terminal object adjoined (cone), so that L_A is the homotopy-colimit cone. But then no functor B^ → A^ exists in general, so the Yoneda reading fits the notation better. Grothendieck crossed all this out, presumably in favour of directly postulating adjoints f_! ⊣ f^* (the later Der 3).
errors: If A^ = Â is the presheaf category, it is not small, so H(Â) is not defined for a 2-functor on small Cat. Size issues (universes, or restriction to a small subcategory of Â) are not addressed. This may be one reason the passage was struck out.

Commutativity 'à isomorphisme près' without specified coherent isomorphisms does not make f_! functorial or pseudo-functorial in f. Uniqueness of f_! and its adjointness to f^* are not stated in the crossed-out version.
Axiom (2) is left blank, so the list of axioms on this page is incomplete.

ideas.what: Underlying-diagram functor α_A : H(A) → Hom(A, H(e)), natural in A (diagram 5)
ideas.modern_name: dia / underlying diagram functor of a (pre)derivator
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Les Dérivateurs); also Heller's homotopy theories, Franke

ideas.what: Der 1: H sends coproducts of categories to products
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck; Heller (1988) has an analogous axiom

ideas.what: Crossed-out approach: postulate an extension L_A : H(A) → H(Â) along the Yoneda embedding with ε^*L_A = id, and define f_! by L_B f_! ≅ (f^*)^*_H L_A, i.e. Kan extensions obtained from pullback along presheaf restriction
ideas.modern_name: Kan extension via the coend formula / Yoneda (free cocompletion) extension; v^* ⊣ u^* transport of adjunctions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Kan 1958; free cocompletion via presheaves). Its use as an axiom pattern for derivators is not standard.
ideas.where_published: unsure; not in this form in Les Dérivateurs as far as I know

missed.claim: An early, abandoned axiomatization of homotopy Kan extensions in a derivator. It reduces the existence of f_! to a single 'Yoneda extension' L_A into presheaf categories plus mere pullback functoriality. This is an alternative formulation of Der3 not in the derivator literature, but it was dropped because of size and coherence issues.
missed.quote: Der 3 ∀ f : A → B dans (Cat), ∃ f_! : H(A) → H(B) telle qu'on ait commutativité à isomorphisme près ... (f^*_∧)^*_H =def f̂_!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents the genesis of the derivator axioms (1983, years before Les Dérivateurs). It connects mildly to later 'derivators on large/accessible diagram shapes' and to Yoneda/cocompletion characterisations of homotopy theories. It is historical rather than mathematically new.

deep.surprise_reason: Early draft of standard derivator axioms. The crossed-out Yoneda-extension formulation of Der3 is a nice historical detail, but it is mathematically classical (coend formula) and was abandoned.
transcription_corrections: The circled label is 'Der 1' and the next circled '(2)' starts an unfinished axiom Der 2. The parenthesis after it is illegible ('(intégration?)' is uncertain).
The struck line probably reads 'Pour toute A ∈ Ob Cat, on donne', with an inserted, crossed-out 'f : A → B'. 'A fibrée' is doubtful.
The bottom arrow in (5) is f^*_{(Hot_H)} : Hom(B, Hot_H) → Hom(A, Hot_H), with underlined Hom.
In (7) the second arrow is labelled (ε_A)^*_H (an earlier label is overwritten), and the curved arrow is id_{H(A)}.
Label 'Der 2' is written near (7), partly overwritten; 'Der 3' heads (8).
